name: find_things_to_do
description:
The tool to reach for whenever someone asks what to do, where to go, what is on, or wants a day or an evening planned.

Send what they said, in their words. When they named what they want, send just that: their tastes would pull the answer off the direction they chose. When the ask is open, add what you know about them that would change which plans are right — who they are, what they have liked, disliked or already done, who they are with. Either way, say what they cannot do or must avoid. One call. We read everything on in that window and that area — a thousand rows and more — and return the ones that fit, in order, each with a sentence saying why it is there.

DO NOT split the request into searches, and do not re-rank or filter what comes back. The ordering is the answer: it was made by reading every candidate against this person's actual request, which is work no selection from a results list can redo. Show them in the order given.

Keyword searches miss the local life — a Go night at a cafe, a running club, an origami meetup, a free park tour — because
none of it describes itself in the words anyone would search for. Reading every row is how those are found.

New York and the San Francisco Bay Area only for now. If they have not said which city, ask them first; an ask with no place is answered with that question.

8-12 seconds for a screenful (the first 50 results) with reasons, 3-6 seconds without; a larger `limit` is what makes it slower.

request.description:
What they want, in their own words. Whether to add what you know about them depends on the ask.

WHEN THEY NAMED WHAT THEY WANT — "jazz tonight" — send that and leave their tastes out: anything you add pulls the answer off the direction they chose.

WHEN THE ASK IS OPEN — "what should we do tonight" — what you know is how the answer finds its direction. Add what would change which plans are right this time: who they are, what they have liked, disliked or already done, who they are with, the occasion. Leave out what does not bear on it.

EITHER WAY, say what they cannot do or must avoid — a wheelchair, an allergy, a budget, "her parents can't be on their feet long". It rules plans out without moving the direction, and is read and reasoned about, never matched as text.

Prose, not keywords, at most 700 characters, their own sentence first, all of it in their voice — "I", "my partner and I", never "they", which reads as someone else coming along. A bare question is fine; there is nothing to invent.

Time and place can be said here too, in words — "tonight", "this weekend", "near Columbia" — and are resolved against the real clock and map. Use the structured fields instead only when you already hold the exact values.

place.description: A place they named — neighbourhood, borough, city, landmark or address — when you hold it exactly. Say where ONE way: this, or the place in `request`, or `lat`/`lng`. Two ways that name different places are not searched; the answer asks which one.

lat.description: Their position, for "near me" / "around here". Send both `lat` and `lng`; either alone is ignored. Only when they want to search around where they are: then name no place in `request` or `place`. A position and a different named place are not searched; the answer asks which one.

lng.description: The other half of `lat`. Negative in the United States.

radius_mi.description: How far they will go. Default 3 miles from a point, 5 from a named area.

when.description: A window you have already resolved, in the local time of the city asked about. Beats any time in `request`. Give `end` only when there is a real deadline: an absent `end` means the rest of that day, not the coming year.

end.description: Same shape as `start`, e.g. 2026-10-02T23:00. A deadline, not a day: leave it out and the window runs to the end of `start`'s day.

limit.description:
How many to return. Defaults to 20, in order; show them in that order, and leave this field out — the default is almost always the one to send.

A smaller number does not come back sooner. The sentences are written in parallel and released in rank order, so the first card arrives at the same moment whether you asked for 12 or 50.

So send a number only when the person wants a short list — never to go faster, because there is no faster here.

cursor.description: Next page of the same answer.

reasons.description: Leave this out: each result comes with a sentence saying why it fits, and that sentence is what to show the person. Send false only when you will not show it — the ranked results come back alone. A next page keeps the first page's choice.

name: get_details
description:
The full record behind a search result, by its id. A search row is a summary; this is everything we hold about that one thing — its whole schedule rather than the next dates, the venue as a place rather than an address, and where else it is listed.

Call it when the row in front of you does not answer what you are about to say. Several ids can go in one call. Not for pictures — the search row already carries the image URL, and this returns none.

items.description: The results to look up, up to 20 at once. One entry per id.

id.description: The id shown on a search result.
